title: Decision Dashboard
subtitle: Review each card and choose A, B, or C.

cards.title: Automatic resend for failed receipt notifications

background.situation: Seven paying users did not receive a receipt notification yesterday after temporary device delivery failures.
background.pain: Without a retry decision, users can wait 6 hours or request refunds because they do not know whether payment succeeded.
background.divergence: The choice decides whether recovery is automatic, operator-led, or user-triggered.

cards.judgment_question: Should every user receive the receipt within 1 hour, or is a daily operator batch acceptable?

options.label: Automatic resend - users receive receipts within 1 hour and operators handle 0 manual cases
Operator batch - missed receipts are handled once per day and users wait around 6 hours
User-triggered retry - users see a failure notice and request resend themselves

cards.title: Retry attempt cap

background.situation: Automatic resend can keep trying while a receiving device remains unavailable.
background.pain: Without a cap, one user's notification can create 20 or more attempts and raise delivery cost above the normal budget.
background.divergence: A low cap protects cost while a high cap improves recovery during temporary failures.

cards.judgment_question: How many attempts within 1 hour best balances recovery and cost?

options.label: 3 attempts - conservative cost and about 70 percent temporary-failure recovery
5 attempts - higher recovery with about 1.7 times delivery cost
Unlimited attempts - maximum recovery but no cost control
